steps: Fill the pasta pot with water and bring it to the boil on the hob.
While the water heats, finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the saucepan over medium-high heat. Brown the beef mince in two batches, breaking it up, for 6–8 minutes.
Lower to medium heat, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, season well and simmer gently for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Salt the boiling water and cook the spaghetti for 9–10 minutes until al dente. Reserve 120ml of pasta water, drain, then toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan steams the mince grey instead of browning it, so cook it in two batches.
Burnt garlic turns bitter, so add it only after the onion has softened and cook it for 1 minute.
Rinsing the spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Stir a splash of the starchy pasta water into the sauce at the end to make it glossy and help it coat the spaghetti.

steps: Fill the large pot with water and put it on the hob to boil with a generous pinch of salt.
While the water heats, finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the saucepan over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the beef mince over high heat, breaking it up, and brown for 8–10 minutes until no pink remains. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and pepper, then simmer on low for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the spaghetti for 10 minutes, or as the packet says, until al dente. Reserve a mugful of pasta water, drain, and toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with mince steams it grey instead of browning it, so use high heat and let it colour.
Simmering the sauce for less than 20 minutes leaves it thin and acidic, so let it reduce until thick.
Rinsing the cooked spaghetti washes off the starch, so the sauce slides off instead of clinging.
output.tip: Toss the drained spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of the pasta water so it coats every strand.

steps: Boil a large pan of salted water on the hob, ready for the spaghetti.
While the water heats, finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the beef mince; brown over high heat for 8–10 minutes, breaking up lumps.
Stir in the tomatoes, season well and simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Cook the spaghetti for 10–11 minutes until al dente, reserve a mugful of pasta water, drain, then toss with the sauce.
pitfalls: Crowding the pan with mince makes it steam and turn grey instead of browning, so use high heat and a wide pan.
Rushing the simmer leaves a thin, acidic sauce, so give it at least 20 minutes.
Rinsing the cooked spaghetti washes off the starch and stops the sauce clinging.
output.tip: Finish the pasta in the sauce with a splash of the reserved pasta water so it turns glossy and coats every strand.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces before heating the pan.
Heat the olive oil in the frying pan over medium heat. Fry the onion and pepper for 6–8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes with a good pinch of salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauce uncovered for 8–10 minutes, until thick enough to leave a trail when you drag a spoon through it.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still wobble.
While the eggs cook, slice the bread and warm it in a toaster or under the grill for 2–3 minutes.
pitfalls: Adding the eggs to a thin, watery sauce makes them sink and spread, so reduce the tomatoes first.
Cooking the eggs on high heat or for too long gives rubbery whites and hard yolks, so keep the heat low and check early.
Skipping the seasoning before simmering leaves the tomato sauce flat and slightly sharp, so season at the tomato stage.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it into the sauce gently and avoid broken yolks.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces before heating the pan.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat, then fry the onion and pepper for 6–8 minutes until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt.
Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes until thick enough to leave a trail when you drag a spoon through it.
Make four wells in the sauce, crack in the eggs, cover and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes until the whites are set.
While the eggs cook, slice the bread and warm it in a toaster or under the grill; serve straight from the pan.
pitfalls: Adding the eggs to thin, watery sauce makes them sink and the whites spread, so reduce the sauce first.
Cooking the eggs on high heat leaves rubbery whites and hard yolks, so keep the heat low and the lid on.
Skipping the seasoning leaves the tomato sauce flat and acidic, so taste and season before adding the eggs.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small bowl first so you can slide it into the sauce without breaking the yolk.

steps: Dice the onion and red pepper into 1cm pieces before heating the pan.
Heat the oil in the frying pan over medium heat, then fry the onion and pepper for 6–8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and season with salt and pepper.
Simmer the sauce for 8–10 minutes, until thick enough to leave a trail when you drag a spoon through it.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack in the eggs. Cover and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes, until the whites are set.
While the eggs cook, slice the bread and warm it in a toaster or under the grill. Serve straight from the pan.
pitfalls: Adding the eggs to thin, watery sauce makes them sink and the whites spread, so reduce the sauce first.
Cooking the eggs on a high heat or for too long leaves the yolks hard, so keep the heat low and check from 5 minutes.
Skipping the lid leaves the egg tops raw while the bases overcook, so cover the pan.
output.tip: Crack each egg into a small cup first so you can slide it into the sauce without breaking the yolk.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Rub the beef with oil, crushed garlic, rosemary, thyme and pepper, then roast for 20 minutes.
Lower the oven to 180°C and roast the beef for a further 60–70 minutes for medium. Rest it under foil for 30 minutes.
While the beef starts, peel and cut the potatoes, parboil for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake roughly. Heat oil in the deep tray.
Roast the potatoes and peeled, halved parsnips and carrots in hot oil for 60–70 minutes, turning once halfway.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and a pinch of salt into a batter and rest it for 30 minutes. Heat oil in the tin at 220°C for 10 minutes, then pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes.
While the beef rests, deglaze its tin with the wine, add stock and simmer for 10 minutes. Steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven during the first 15 minutes of baking makes the Yorkshire puddings collapse, so keep the door shut.
Carving the beef without a 30-minute rest releases the juices and leaves the meat dry.
Adding batter to lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so wait until the oil is smoking hot.
output.tip: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour before roasting so it cooks evenly, and pull it at 52°C in the centre for medium-rare.

steps: Take the beef out of the fridge 1 hour before cooking, then rub with oil, salt, pepper, crushed garlic, rosemary and thyme.
Heat the oven to 220°C and roast the beef for 20 minutes. Reduce to 180°C and cook for 1 hour 10 minutes for medium (60°C core).
While the beef cooks, peel and cut the potatoes, parboil for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake roughly. Whisk the flour, eggs and milk into a smooth batter and rest it.
Heat oil in the roasting tray, add the potatoes and roast at 200°C for 60 minutes, turning once. Add the parsnips and carrots with butter for the final 40 minutes.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Raise the oven to 230°C, heat oil in the Yorkshire tin until smoking, pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes.
Deglaze the roasting tin on the hob with the wine, then simmer with the stock for 10 minutes. Steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven door while the Yorkshire puddings rise makes them collapse and turn flat and soggy.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
Putting potatoes into lukewarm fat gives pale, greasy roasties, so make sure the oil is sizzling hot first.
output.tip: Roast the beef on a rack of halved onions so the base does not stew and the pan juices turn into richer gravy.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and take the beef out of the fridge. Rub it with oil, salt, pepper, rosemary and thyme, then sear in the roasting tin on the hob for 5 minutes.
Roast the beef at 220°C for 20 minutes, then lower to 180°C. Cook for about 1 hour 10 minutes to 55°C in the centre for medium-rare.
While the beef starts, parboil the potatoes for 8–10 minutes, drain and shake roughly. Mix the batter and rest it for at least 30 minutes.
Roast the potatoes and parsnips in hot oil on the tray at 200°C for 50–60 minutes, turning once. Add the carrots and garlic after 20 minutes.
Rest the beef under foil for 30 minutes. Raise the oven to 220°C, heat oil in the pudding tin for 10 minutes, then pour in the batter and bake for 20–25 minutes.
While the puddings bake, deglaze the roasting tin with wine and stock, then simmer for 10 minutes. Steam the broccoli for 4–5 minutes, then carve the beef and serve with horseradish.
pitfalls: Opening the oven while the Yorkshire puddings rise makes them collapse, so keep the door shut for 20 minutes.
Putting the batter into lukewarm fat gives flat, greasy puddings, so heat the oil until it is smoking hot first.
Carving the beef straight from the oven lets the juices run out and leaves the meat dry, so rest it for 30 minutes.
output.tip: Roughen the parboiled potatoes in the colander and put them into preheated oil so the edges turn extra crisp.

pitfalls: Browning chicken straight from the yoghurt marinade with lots of clinging liquid makes it steam rather than colour, so scrape off the excess and brown in two batches.
Adding the tomatoes and simmering without tasting means the sauce can turn sharp and acidic, so season with salt and a pinch of sugar near the end.
Cooking the rice without rinsing it first leaves it gluey and clumpy, so rinse 300g until the water runs almost clear.
output.tip: Finish the curry with a spoonful of yoghurt or a splash of double cream and a pinch of garam masala off the heat for a rounder, more fragrant sauce.

pitfalls: Adding the tomatoes straight after browning leaves charred marinade stuck to the pan, which turns bitter; deglaze with a splash of water and scrape it up first.
Simmering at a hard boil splits the yoghurt into grainy curds and toughens the chicken, so keep the heat low enough for gentle bubbles only.
Cooking the rice without rinsing it, or stirring it while it cooks, gives sticky, clumped grains instead of fluffy ones; rinse until the water runs clear and leave the lid on.
output.tip: Start the rice when the chicken goes into the sauce, then finish the curry with a squeeze of lemon juice and a handful of chopped coriander to lift the flavour.

pitfalls: Adding the chicken with its wet marinade straight to the pan makes it stew rather than brown, so scrape off the excess yoghurt first and brown in two batches.
Pouring cold yoghurt-coated chicken into a boiling sauce can make the yoghurt split and look grainy, so keep the simmer gentle at a low bubble.
Cooking rice without rinsing it and without a measured water ratio gives sticky or uneven grains, so rinse 300g until the water runs clear and use about 450ml water.
output.tip: Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and a handful of chopped coriander off the heat to lift the flavour of the sauce.

pitfalls: Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water for too long, or adding them to the wok still dripping, makes them mushy and clumpy; soak until just pliable, drain well and toss with a little oil.
Adding the soy sauce straight onto the noodles in one spot makes them salty in patches and dark in colour; pour it around the edge of the wok and toss quickly.
Cutting the broccoli into large, uneven florets leaves some raw and others overcooked; cut them to about 3cm and blanch for 1 minute, or add a splash of water and cover briefly.
output.tip: Add a small splash of rice vinegar or lime juice off the heat to lift the soy and keep the cornstarch coating tasting bright.

pitfalls: Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water for too long, or cooking them fully before the wok, leaves them mushy and clumpy; soak until just pliable, drain well and toss with a little oil.
Adding all the soy sauce straight onto the noodles makes them stick and turn unevenly salty; mix it with 2–3 tbsp of water first and pour it around the edge of the wok.
Cutting the broccoli into large, uneven florets leaves some pieces raw while others overcook; cut them to about 3cm and keep the red pepper in similar-sized strips.
output.tip: Add a splash of water to the wok and cover for 1 minute after the broccoli goes in, so it steams to tender-crisp without needing extra oil.

pitfalls: Soaking the rice noodles in boiling water for too long, or cooking them fully before the wok, leaves them soft and prone to breaking up; soak until just pliable, then drain well.
Pouring all the soy sauce straight onto the hot wok makes it burn and turn bitter, and the noodles clump; mix it with 2–3 tbsp of water first and add it off the heat's peak.
Crowding the pan when frying the tofu steams it instead of crisping it; fry in two batches so the cubes don't touch.
output.tip: Cut the broccoli into small, even florets and add 2 tbsp of water with a lid on for 1 minute, so the stalks turn tender without overcooking the red pepper.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees, kuni alustad ülejäänud tööd, ja nõruta enne keetmist.
Lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks ja haki sibul peeneks.
Prae liha potis kuumas rasvas pruuniks, lisa sibul ja prae veel 3–4 minutit.
Lisa nõrutatud hapukapsas, odrakruubid, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et kate on peaaegu kaetud, ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 1 tund.
Koori ja tükelda kartulid ning lisa potti, kui kruubid ja kapsas on pooleldi pehmed, siis hauta veel 30–40 minutit.
Sega aeg-ajalt, lisa vajadusel vett ja maitsesta sooläga, kuni kruubid on pehmed ja roog paks.
pitfalls: Ära soola enne hapukapsa maitsmist: hapukapsas on juba soolane ja roog läheb liiga soolaseks.
Ära jäta potti järelevalveta ilma vedelikku kontrollimata: kruubid imavad vee endasse ja roog kõrbeb põhja.
Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja roog kaotab tekstuuri.
output.tip: Mulgikapsad maitsevad järgmisel päeval veel paremini, kui lasta neil üle öö hästi läbi tõmmata ja siis uuesti soojendada.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees vähemalt 1 tund, parem üleöö, ja nõruta enne kasutamist.
Haki sibul ja lõika sealiha 3 cm kuubikuteks.
Prae liha potis kuumal rasval igast küljest pruuniks, lisa sibul ja prae 2–3 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa nõrutatud hapukapsas, odrakruubid, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab poole potist. Kuumuta keemiseni, keera kuumus madalaks ja hauta kaane all 1,5 tundi.
Kooli ja tükelda kartulid 3 cm tükkideks ning lisa potti, kui hautamisest on jäänud umbes 40 minutit.
Hauta, kuni kruubid ja kartul on pehmed ning liha laguneb kahvliga. Sega aeg-ajalt ja lisa vajadusel kuuma vett.
pitfalls: Ära jäta odrakruupe leotamata: need jäävad kõvaks ja hautamine venib tunde pikemaks.
Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja kapsahautis kaotab ilme.
Ära jäta potti järelevalveta ilma vedelikku kontrollimata: kruubid imavad vett ja hautis kõrbeb põhja.
output.tip: Hauta mulgikapsaid ahjus 160 °C juures kaanega potis, siis ei kõrbe põhi ja maitsed segunevad ühtlaselt.

steps: Leota odrakruupe külmas vees ja loputa need enne keetmist kurnis läbi.
Haki sealiha 3 cm tükkideks ja sibul peeneks.
Prae sealiha potis kuumas rasvas kõigilt külgedelt pruuniks, lisa sibul ja prae 3–4 minutit pehmeks.
Lisa hapukapsas, odrakruubid, loorberilehed ja nii palju vett, et see katab poole sisust, ning hauta kaane all madalal kuumusel 1,5 tundi.
Koori kartulid, lõika need 3 cm tükkideks ja lisa potti, kui hautamist on jäänud umbes 30–40 minutit.
Sega aeg-ajalt läbi, lisa vajadusel vett ja maitsesta soolaga. Eemalda loorberilehed enne serveerimist.
pitfalls: Ära lisa kartuleid liiga vara: need keevad pudruks ja roog kaotab oma tekstuuri.
Ära jäta potti ilma järelevalveta ega kuumuta liiga kõrgel: kruubid kleepuvad põhja külge kinni ja kõrbevad.
Ära soola enne hautamise lõppu: hapukapsas ja liha annavad ise soolasust ning roog võib minna liiga soolaseks.
output.tip: Lase valmis mulgikapsastel enne serveerimist 10 minutit kaane all seista, siis imavad kruubid maitsed paremini sisse.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksemaks kui 5 mm: paksemad viilud jäävad 20 minutiga seest toorteks, õhemad aga kuivavad ja kõrbevad ära.
Ära pane kartuleid ahju kuivalt: ilma oliiviõlita ja soolata kleepuvad viilud plaadi külge ning jäävad maitsetuks ja kahvatuks.
Ära pane lõhet kartulitele külmkapikülmalt ja nahk üleval märjalt: külm kala küpseb ebaühtlaselt ning märg pind aurutab, selle asemel et kergelt pruunistuda.
output.tip: Kontrolli lõhe küpsust 15. minutil: kala on valmis, kui paksem koht on 56–58 °C ja liha laguneb kahvliga kihiti, siis ei jää see kuiv.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile ilma õlita: ilma oliiviõli või muu õlita kleepuvad need plaadi külge ja jäävad kuivaks.
Ära lõika kartuliviile liiga paksuks (üle 5 mm): 20 minutiga ei küpse need läbi ja lõhe on enne valmis kui kartul.
Ära pane lõhet ahju külmkapikülmalt ja nahk allpool märjana: lõhe küpseb ebaühtlaselt ja nahk jääb limaseks, kuivata filee enne paberiga.
output.tip: Lõika lõhe 3 portsjoniks ja kontrolli küpsust, kui filee paksuim koht on 60 °C juures või muutub kahvliga hõlpsasti kihiliseks, siis jääb kala mahlane.

pitfalls: Ära jäta kartuliviile paksemaks kui 5 mm: paksemad viilud ei küpse 20 minutiga läbi ja jäävad keskelt toored.
Ära pane kartuleid ahju kuiva ja maitsestamata kujul: ilma õli ja soolata jäävad viilud kuivaks ning maitsetuks.
Ära pane külmkapikülmat lõhet otse kuumadele kartulitele: väliskiht kuivab ära enne, kui sisu küpseb, nii et kuiva kala saab sul lihtsalt.
output.tip: Kuivata lõhefilee paberrätikuga ja lase toasooja 10 minutit seista, siis küpseb see ühtlasemalt ning jääb mahlaseks.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulatatud võid kuumalt taigna sisse: muna hakkab osaliselt hanguma ja taina sisse jäävad tükikesed.
Ära pane taigna sisse korraga kogu jahu ilma vispeldamata: tekivad ttükid, mida hiljem raske lahti saada.
Ära keera pann liiga kuumaks ega küpseta esimest pannkooki enne, kui pann on korralikult soojenenud: taigen kas kõrbeb pealt või jääb kleepuma ja rebeneb ümberpööramisel.
output.tip: Määri pann õhukeselt võiga ainult esimese pannkoogi jaoks, sest taignas on juba või ja järgmised ei kleepu, ning vala 60–70 ml taent korraga ja keera pann kiiresti ringi, siis jäävad koogid ühtlaselt õhukesed.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulatatud võid taignasse kuumana: see võib muna osaliselt kinni keeta ja tainas jääb tükiline.
Ära küpseta liiga kuumal pannil: pannkoogi servad pruunistuvad enne, kui keskosa kuivab, ja koogid rebenevad keeramisel.
Ära vala pannile liiga palju taignat korraga: koogid jäävad paksuks ja kummised, mitte õhukesed ja pitsilised.
output.tip: Esimene pannkook on proovikook: kui see jääb liiga paks, lisa taignale 30–50 ml piima, ja kui rebeneb, lase taignal veel 5 minutit seista.

pitfalls: Ära vala sulatatud võid kuumalt taignasse: muna hakkab kokku tõmbuma ja taignasse jäävad tombud.
Ära küpseta pannkooke liiga kuumal pannil: pealt jääb tainas totoreks, alt kõrbeb ära ja keskelt jääb toores.
Ära keera pannkooki ümber enne, kui serv on kuiv ja pind kaotab läikiva märja välimuse: koogid rebenevad ja kleepuvad pannile.
output.tip: Määri pann esimese pannkoogi jaoks õhukeselt võiga ja vala pannile umbes 60 ml taignat, siis keeruta pann kiiresti ringi, et tainas jaotuks õhukeseks ja ühtlaseks kihiks.
